We provide a competitive compensation package that recognizes your experience, credentials, and education alongside a robust benefits program to meet your needs. Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several US geographic markets.

Who We Are

Since 1954, Cupertino Electric, Inc. (CEI) has been powered by people who’ve built a reputation for delivering high-profile, complex projects. Real, tangible things that alter the landscape and improve lives. And we've done it with integrity for more than 70 years. We’re problem solvers and innovation seekers. We’re team players and safety fanatics. And we're proud to be part of Quanta Services (PWR:NYSE), North America's largest employer of skilled craft labor. Because what we do is important, but how we do it is everything.

THE MODULAR TEAM

Modular solutions by CEI anticipate and solve ongoing problems for data center operators. Our proven, factory-built and tested data center infrastructure products bring deployments online faster, more reliably, and with less risk than conventional methods.

About The Role

We're seeking a Project Coordinator ready to be on the front lines of a project, giving daily support to field, project management, and customer teams. This role regularly communicates with field and safety professionals ensuring proper the flow of information such as tracking payroll times for the Production team and processing all new hire enrollment documentation. The Coordinator will assist in WO processing and proposal, bid presentation, change orders, submittals, and RFI & RFD document processing. Other responsibilities include maintaining and updating job files and controlled forms/logs. You’ll provide coordination and administrative support for project managers including tracking schedule, setting up meetings and organizing travel and catering.

You have a love for order and organization. Working in a fast-paced environment is familiar, and you are flexible and able to adjust to changing situations. You are a natural when it comes to communication and can be seen as “the glue that holds a project together.” You have exceptional communication, writing and organizational skills. Most of all, you're passionate about upholding Cupertino Electric's values of integrity, safety, excellence, innovation, and people, learning relevant aspects of the business, and being an asset to your team.

Excellent communication, written, and organizational skills.
Adaptable and flexible paired with critical thinking and reasoning skills.
Strong understanding of software such as Zoom to manage online group presentations and calls.
Solid experience with Microsoft Office Suite – Word and Excel.

What You Will Gain

As a Project Coordinator, you will play a key role in the operations of a construction project. You will interact and engage with our project teams and field personnel – allowing you to get an understanding of the partnership that takes place behind-the-scenes to ensure the success of a project. jobs.title: Program Coordinator II, Community Based Research Initiative (Community Engagement & Research Coordination)
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Under the general supervision of the Executive Director and Program Principal Investigator, the INSPIRE Programs Coordinator will manage the day-to-day operations of CDU’s growing portfolio of INSPIRE community-based research programs—INSPIRE Faith, INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA. The Coordinator serves as the primary operational point of contact across these programs, combining research-program coordination, community relationship-building, and oversight of the digital engagement and data-capture platforms (in partnership with the technology team) that enable the programs to operate at scale. The role blends hands-on, place-based community partnership (primarily through INSPIRE Faith) with the coordination of predominantly online, largely automated statewide, and national programs. A central purpose of the role is to strengthen community trust in research and to broaden the participation of Black/African American/Hispanic communities and other communities of color in clinical research and trials, ensuring that community voice and priorities shape how the work is designed and carried out.

About The Center

The Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science (CDU), a partner in the UCLA Clinical and Translational Science Institute (CTSI) alongside UCLA and Cedars-Sinai, is building a community-centered clinical research enterprise through its Clinical and Translational Research Center (CTRC) in South Los Angeles. The INSPIRE programs are a family of community-based research initiatives advancing health and brain health across diverse populations. INSPIRE Faith is a deep, place-based partnership with faith institutions requiring regular in-person engagement with community partners; INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA are digitally delivered, largely automated programs conducted primarily online, with select live sessions led by physicians and study staff. Together they build on CDU’s longstanding legacy of community engagement and health-equity research.

This work advances a national commitment to health equity: expanding access to healthcare in underserved communities, building lasting trust between communities of color and the healthcare system, and increasing the participation of Black/African American communities and other communities of color in research and clinical trials. As a historically Black graduate institution, CDU pursues these goals in partnership with peer institutions and community organizations, treating community relationships not as a means of recruitment but as the foundation of research that is shaped by, accountable to, and beneficial for the communities it serves. The INSPIRE Programs Coordinator is central to this mission, serving as the trusted community bridge that connects faith and community partners to research and trial opportunities and helps ensure that the science reflects the priorities of the community.

Essential Duties

Manage the day-to-day operations and coordination of the INSPIRE research programs (Faith, CA, and USA), ensuring each program runs smoothly, on schedule, and in alignment with study protocols and the Center’s mission
Coordinate in-person activities for INSPIRE Faith—anticipated at approximately two days per week of on-site engagement with community partners—and support the logistics of live sessions conducted by physicians and study staff across all programs, including scheduling, participant coordination, and event execution.
Coordinate and support program staff, students, and volunteers across the INSPIRE programs, including onboarding, task coordination, and training
Support participant recruitment, retention, and outreach across programs, including coordinating culturally appropriate promotional and educational materials (in collaboration with the communications team)
Attend community meetings, faith-partner gatherings, health events, and program activities as needed to represent the INSPIRE programs and CDU
Oversee the online engagement platform, participant communications, scheduled calls, and data-capture elements for the digitally delivered programs (INSPIRE CA, and USA), coordinating closely with the technology team to ensure the platforms function reliably and participant data is captured accurately and securely.
Monitor program metrics, participant engagement, and feedback to assess effectiveness, support quality improvement, and inform recommendations to program leadership
Establish and support Faith Community Advisory Boards across Los Angeles, coordinating the formation of one board in 2026 and several additional boards by 2028. Each board is a governance body of no more than 11 faith leaders drawn from partnering faith institutions, guiding program direction, protocol input, and community voice at the faith-partner level.
The Coordinator organizes board recruitment, scheduling, meeting logistics, and ongoing stewardship.

Recruit, onboard, and support Community Navigators from partnering faith institutions, growing the Navigator corps to 50 by the end of 2026 and more than 500 by the end of 2028. Navigators are community members who support the conduct of the studies from the faith-community side, including participant recruitment, guidance in navigating different community and clinical spaces, and support at program events.
Navigators are distinct from advisory board members and are not study participants themselves.

Organize and help lead faith-based health festivals, coordinating planning, faith-partner engagement, logistics, staffing, and execution to advance community health and program visibility across partnering faith institutions.
Build trusted partnerships with community and faith-based organizations, serving as the primary liaison and fostering ongoing engagement across INSPIRE programs.
Advance community-centered research by connecting partners to clinical research opportunities, promoting diverse participation, and ensuring community voices inform program and study design through transparent and culturally responsive engagement.
Perform administrative tasks related to community engagement program management, such as creating reports, PowerPoint, and maintaining records
Support grant management and reporting for the programs—including tracking deliverables, timelines, and compliance, and coordinating with dedicated grant writers who lead proposal writing (this role is not responsible for writing grants)

Education

Required Qualifications

Four-year college degree (B.A., B.S.) in Health Sciences. Experience in Business Administration, Public Administration, or Public Health is an advantage.

Experience

At least 2 or more years of experience coordinating research programs, studies, or educational/community programs, preferably in an academic, clinical research, or healthcare setting and activities.
Experience with grant or program management, including tracking deliverables, timelines, budgets, and reporting requirements for federal, local, or private funders (proposal writing is handled by dedicated grant writers and is not required for this role).
Experience in coordination of staff and students, including experience working in conjunction with HR. Also strongly prefer experience working with diverse partners and cultural sensitivity.
Demonstrated ability to build and sustain trusted relationships with community members, faith-based or community organizations, and diverse partners; experience with community-engaged or community-based work strongly preferred.
Understanding of, and commitment to, expanding access to healthcare and increasing the participation of Black/African American communities and other communities of color in clinical research and trials; familiarity with the trust barriers that affect research participation in underserved communities and with community-centered approaches to addressing them strongly preferred.
Experience recruiting, organizing, and supporting community advisory boards, community health workers or navigators, and community volunteers, ideally within faith-based settings; experience planning or leading community or faith-based health events or festivals strongly preferred.
Comfort with technology and digital tools; experience using online engagement platforms, virtual meeting/call coordination, databases, or electronic data-capture systems (e.g., REDCap) preferred. Ability to work closely with a technology team to support program platforms and data workflows.
Experience with developing and communicating, in written and oral form, detailed and technical scientific and administrative program information to various audiences.
Has experience developing evaluation metrics to assist Supervisor in reviewing effectiveness of program activities, recommending improvements, and assisting in executing recommendations.
Has experience developing marketing/promotional information to increase visibility of the institution or program. Prefer experience articulating detailed or technical scientific information in a generally publicly acceptable and culturally appropriate manner.
Ability to develop and maintain professional working relationships in complex program/organizational settings involving heterogeneous constituents such as academic and clinical faculty, staff, students, and community partners from diverse backgrounds.
Experience with interpreting operating policies and procedures and resolving minor discipline and other employee relations issues within an academic setting or institution.

Skills

Demonstrated experience developing and executing community engagement strategy
Proven ability to build relationships and partnerships with diverse groups
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Strong organizational and time-management skills
Budget development and oversight experience
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Prefer basic/working knowledge of Spanish language.
Proficient in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
Strong research-program coordination skills, including managing multiple concurrent programs, timelines, and deliverables with attention to protocol and compliance requirements
Comfort with online engagement platforms, virtual meeting tools, and electronic data-capture systems; able to partner effectively with a technology team

Complexity

The ability to perform highly detailed work with sustained attention and care while providing/obtaining information on numerous inquiries is paramount to success in this position.

Long-term sitting at a computer workstation. Frequent standing and walking; occasional standing for multiple hours at events. Finger movement, feeling sufficient to work on computers and equipment; speaking clearly, hearing conversationally, and seeing far and near. Regular off-campus travel will be involved, including approximately two days per week of in-person engagement for INSPIRE Faith.

jobs.description:
Discover Your Career at Emory University

Emory University is a leading research university that fosters excellence and attracts world-class talent to innovate today and prepare leaders for the future. We welcome candidates who can contribute to the excellence of our academic community.

Description

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Creates and maintains a data dictionary and meta data.
Supports efforts to ensure that data standards are developed and maintained.
Ensures that the uses of data through reports and queries are accurate.
Supports business and system re-engineering and architecture development to define future data needs.
Serves as an organizational consultant on matters relating to databases by providing expertise to assist users in meeting their needs.
Performs other related duties as required.

ADDITIONAL JOB DETAILS:

The research team of Dr. Aaron Siegler (Bio: https://sph.emory.edu/profile/faculty/aaron-siegler) in the Epidemiology Department at Emory University is seeking to hire a Data Analyst to work on several NIH-funded studies in HIV prevention epidemiology and digital health intervention research across local and/or international settings.

These studies include:

Establishing a PrEP Epidemiology, Modeling and Surveillance System (PREMISE), a study to support the development of consistent national HIV Pre-ExposureProphylaxis (PrEP) data to describe its patterns of use, and to understand which programs and policies are effective at facilitating PrEP uptake in the US.
Improving telePrEP initiation and retention outcomes in the US: The MISTR+ study, an NIH-funded series of clinical trials to support the development of low-touchinterventions (such as tailored messaging) and testing their effectiveness on PrEP initiation and retention outcomes.
The Elección (Choice) Cohort: Developing and testing a scalable, platform-agnostic digital intervention in Peru, an NIH-funded clinical trial to improve understanding of the factors associated with HIV acquisition and PrEP uptake; and evaluate the preferences for and effectiveness of an adapted digital health messaging intervention (mHealth) among men in Peru.

The Data Analyst will have the opportunity to work on multiple projects as described above, with specific work distribution depending on experience and interests. The Data Analyst may have the opportunity to contribute to other ongoing projects in Dr. Siegler’s research lab, co-author manuscripts, and present scientific work at national/international scientific conferences if interested.

Key responsibilities:

Work closely with the Principal Investigator in all aspects of the research
Develop data collection systems
Conduct data cleaning and codebook development
Monitor study data and provide biweekly updates to the study team on accumulating data
Prepare analysis datasets and documentation
Facilitate study analysis and assist faculty and post-docs in data analysis activities, including table and figure development for manuscripts
Contribute to quantitative research efforts in the field of HIV epidemiology and prevention
Apply statistical models and use statistical software to derive quantitative research findings
Work as part of a team to develop scientific data from various data sources
Contribute as co-author to manuscripts
Contribute to data visualization output to disseminate study findings

The position will be based at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia. The initial appointment is for 2 years, and renewal is anticipated if performance is satisfactory and funds remain available.

Detailed Project Description:

PREMISE

To reach Ending the Epidemic (ETE) targets, we will need consistent national HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) data to describe patterns of use and to understand which programs and policies are effective at facilitating PrEP uptake. This NIH-funded study aims to build on our history of developing public PrEP data resources and innovative metrics of PrEP use in PREMISE (PrEP Epidemiology, Modeling, and Surveillance), a collaborative and interdisciplinary group that will use national PrEP data, along with legal and policy coding, to inform the US HIV epidemic response. The study will conduct analyses regarding the scope of PrEP scale-up over time and will perform analyses to explore the impact of different locality-specific programs and policies on PrEP use

MISTR+

Our study (MISTR+) seeks to establish an evidence base for telehealth and improve health outcomes in terms of PrEP care initiation, retention, and re-engagement for the over 100,000 users of this service by (1) developing a series of low-touch interventions based on existing evidence and new data analyses of telePrEP electronic records data, (2) testing interventions, and (3) enhancing our understanding of intervention performance through machine learning and cost-effectiveness analysesthat will inform intervention prioritization.

Elección

The HIV epidemic in Latin America is concentrated among MSM. As the number of HIV prevention options grows, it is critical to build interventions that empower individuals to make HIV prevention choices that fit their lives; this requires delineating and addressing barriers, elucidating individual preferences, and providing accessible prevention options. Remote access to health services and information may overcome many challenges of traditional clinic service delivery models. TheElección study will improve our understanding of health determinants for HIV incidence and the prevention and care cascades in Peru. The study will build a cohort to assess HIV incidence and its predictors and to identify intervention preferences. We will adapt and test a digital intervention grounded in participant choice to improve HIV prevention service uptake. Specifically, we will develop an observational HIV incidence cohort (Aim 1), implement discrete choice experiments and use the ADAPT-ITT model to inform adaptation of an evidence-based intervention to the Peruvian setting (Aim 2), and transition cohort members into the clinical trial (Aim 3). Participants will be randomized to either the adapted version of the digital intervention (M-Cubicado) or to observation-only follow-up (standard of care).

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

A bachelor's degree and one year of experience in data analysis, statistics, or a related field, OR an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Master’s degree in Epidemiology, Biostatistics or other relevant quantitative field.
Experience with quantitative data analysis.
Experience using statistical software to derive quantitative research findings.
Excellent scientific writing ability
Experience in data management and analysis using SAS, R or other statistical software.
Experience in analysis of clinical trial and/or national claims data.
Experience in HIV prevention or digital health

NOTE: This role will be granted the opportunity to work from home regularly but must be able to commute to Emory University on a flexible weekly schedule based upon business needs. Schedule is based on agreed upon guidelines of department. This role requires residency in the state of GA. Emory reserves the right to change remote work status with notice to employee.

new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

Under the general supervision of the Executive Director and Program Principal Investigator, the INSPIRE Programs Coordinator will manage the day-to-day operations of CDU’s growing portfolio of INSPIRE community-based research programs—INSPIRE Faith, INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA. The Coordinator serves as the primary operational point of contact across these programs, combining research-program coordination, community relationship-building, and oversight of the digital engagement and data-capture platforms (in partnership with the technology team) that enable the programs to operate at scale. The role blends hands-on, place-based community partnership (primarily through INSPIRE Faith) with the coordination of predominantly online, largely automated statewide, and national programs. A central purpose of the role is to strengthen community trust in research and to broaden the participation of Black/African American/Hispanic communities and other communities of color in clinical research and trials, ensuring that community voice and priorities shape how the work is designed and carried out.

About The Center

The Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science (CDU), a partner in the UCLA Clinical and Translational Science Institute (CTSI) alongside UCLA and Cedars-Sinai, is building a community-centered clinical research enterprise through its Clinical and Translational Research Center (CTRC) in South Los Angeles. The INSPIRE programs are a family of community-based research initiatives advancing health and brain health across diverse populations. INSPIRE Faith is a deep, place-based partnership with faith institutions requiring regular in-person engagement with community partners; INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA are digitally delivered, largely automated programs conducted primarily online, with select live sessions led by physicians and study staff. Together they build on CDU’s longstanding legacy of community engagement and health-equity research.

This work advances a national commitment to health equity: expanding access to healthcare in underserved communities, building lasting trust between communities of color and the healthcare system, and increasing the participation of Black/African American communities and other communities of color in research and clinical trials. As a historically Black graduate institution, CDU pursues these goals in partnership with peer institutions and community organizations, treating community relationships not as a means of recruitment but as the foundation of research that is shaped by, accountable to, and beneficial for the communities it serves. The INSPIRE Programs Coordinator is central to this mission, serving as the trusted community bridge that connects faith and community partners to research and trial opportunities and helps ensure that the science reflects the priorities of the community.

Essential Duties

Manage the day-to-day operations and coordination of the INSPIRE research programs (Faith, CA, and USA), ensuring each program runs smoothly, on schedule, and in alignment with study protocols and the Center’s mission
Coordinate in-person activities for INSPIRE Faith—anticipated at approximately two days per week of on-site engagement with community partners—and support the logistics of live sessions conducted by physicians and study staff across all programs, including scheduling, participant coordination, and event execution.
Coordinate and support program staff, students, and volunteers across the INSPIRE programs, including onboarding, task coordination, and training
Support participant recruitment, retention, and outreach across programs, including coordinating culturally appropriate promotional and educational materials (in collaboration with the communications team)
Attend community meetings, faith-partner gatherings, health events, and program activities as needed to represent the INSPIRE programs and CDU
Oversee the online engagement platform, participant communications, scheduled calls, and data-capture elements for the digitally delivered programs (INSPIRE CA, and USA), coordinating closely with the technology team to ensure the platforms function reliably and participant data is captured accurately and securely.
Monitor program metrics, participant engagement, and feedback to assess effectiveness, support quality improvement, and inform recommendations to program leadership
Establish and support Faith Community Advisory Boards across Los Angeles, coordinating the formation of one board in 2026 and several additional boards by 2028. Each board is a governance body of no more than 11 faith leaders drawn from partnering faith institutions, guiding program direction, protocol input, and community voice at the faith-partner level.
The Coordinator organizes board recruitment, scheduling, meeting logistics, and ongoing stewardship.

Recruit, onboard, and support Community Navigators from partnering faith institutions, growing the Navigator corps to 50 by the end of 2026 and more than 500 by the end of 2028. Navigators are community members who support the conduct of the studies from the faith-community side, including participant recruitment, guidance in navigating different community and clinical spaces, and support at program events.
Navigators are distinct from advisory board members and are not study participants themselves.

Organize and help lead faith-based health festivals, coordinating planning, faith-partner engagement, logistics, staffing, and execution to advance community health and program visibility across partnering faith institutions.
Build trusted partnerships with community and faith-based organizations, serving as the primary liaison and fostering ongoing engagement across INSPIRE programs.
Advance community-centered research by connecting partners to clinical research opportunities, promoting diverse participation, and ensuring community voices inform program and study design through transparent and culturally responsive engagement.
Perform administrative tasks related to community engagement program management, such as creating reports, PowerPoint, and maintaining records
Support grant management and reporting for the programs—including tracking deliverables, timelines, and compliance, and coordinating with dedicated grant writers who lead proposal writing (this role is not responsible for writing grants)

Education

Required Qualifications

Four-year college degree (B.A., B.S.) in Health Sciences. Experience in Business Administration, Public Administration, or Public Health is an advantage.

Experience

At least 2 or more years of experience coordinating research programs, studies, or educational/community programs, preferably in an academic, clinical research, or healthcare setting and activities.
Experience with grant or program management, including tracking deliverables, timelines, budgets, and reporting requirements for federal, local, or private funders (proposal writing is handled by dedicated grant writers and is not required for this role).
Experience in coordination of staff and students, including experience working in conjunction with HR. Also strongly prefer experience working with diverse partners and cultural sensitivity.
Demonstrated ability to build and sustain trusted relationships with community members, faith-based or community organizations, and diverse partners; experience with community-engaged or community-based work strongly preferred.

Job Summary:

Under the general supervision of the Executive Director and Program Principal Investigator, the INSPIRE Programs Coordinator will manage the day-to-day operations of CDU’s growing portfolio of INSPIRE community-based research programs—INSPIRE Faith, INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA. The role blends hands-on, place-based community partnership (primarily through INSPIRE Faith) with the coordination of predominantly online, largely automated statewide, and national programs. About the Center:
The Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science (CDU), a partner in the UCLA Clinical and Translational Science Institute (CTSI) alongside UCLA and Cedars-Sinai, is building a community-centered clinical research enterprise through its Clinical and Translational Research Center (CTRC) in South Los Angeles. The INSPIRE programs are a family of community-based research initiatives advancing health and brain health across diverse populations. INSPIRE Faith is a deep, place-based partnership with faith institutions requiring regular in-person engagement with community partners; INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA are digitally delivered, largely automated programs conducted primarily online, with select live sessions led by physicians and study staff. Together they build on CDU’s longstanding legacy of community engagement and health-equity research.

This work advances a national commitment to health equity: expanding access to healthcare in underserved communities, building lasting trust between communities of color and the healthcare system, and increasing the participation of Black/African American communities and other communities of color in research and clinical trials. As a historically Black graduate institution, CDU pursues these goals in partnership with peer institutions and community organizations, treating community relationships not as a means of recruitment but as the foundation of research that is shaped by, accountable to, and beneficial for the communities it serves. Discover Your Career at Emory University

Emory University is a leading research university that fosters excellence and attracts world-class talent to innovate today and prepare leaders for the future. We welcome candidates who can contribute to the excellence of our academic community.

Description

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Creates and maintains a data dictionary and meta data.
Supports efforts to ensure that data standards are developed and maintained.
Ensures that the uses of data through reports and queries are accurate.
Supports business and system re-engineering and architecture development to define future data needs.
Serves as an organizational consultant on matters relating to databases by providing expertise to assist users in meeting their needs.
Performs other related duties as required.

ADDITIONAL JOB DETAILS:

The research team of Dr. Aaron Siegler (Bio: https://sph.emory.edu/profile/faculty/aaron-siegler) in the Epidemiology Department at Emory University is seeking to hire a Data Analyst to work on several NIH-funded studies in HIV prevention epidemiology and digital health intervention research across local and/or international settings.

These studies include:

Establishing a PrEP Epidemiology, Modeling and Surveillance System (PREMISE), a study to support the development of consistent national HIV Pre-ExposureProphylaxis (PrEP) data to describe its patterns of use, and to understand which programs and policies are effective at facilitating PrEP uptake in the US.
Improving telePrEP initiation and retention outcomes in the US: The MISTR+ study, an NIH-funded series of clinical trials to support the development of low-touchinterventions (such as tailored messaging) and testing their effectiveness on PrEP initiation and retention outcomes.
The Elección (Choice) Cohort: Developing and testing a scalable, platform-agnostic digital intervention in Peru, an NIH-funded clinical trial to improve understanding of the factors associated with HIV acquisition and PrEP uptake; and evaluate the preferences for and effectiveness of an adapted digital health messaging intervention (mHealth) among men in Peru.

The Data Analyst will have the opportunity to work on multiple projects as described above, with specific work distribution depending on experience and interests. The Data Analyst may have the opportunity to contribute to other ongoing projects in Dr. Siegler’s research lab, co-author manuscripts, and present scientific work at national/international scientific conferences if interested.

Key responsibilities:

Work closely with the Principal Investigator in all aspects of the research
Develop data collection systems
Conduct data cleaning and codebook development
Monitor study data and provide biweekly updates to the study team on accumulating data
Prepare analysis datasets and documentation
Facilitate study analysis and assist faculty and post-docs in data analysis activities, including table and figure development for manuscripts
Contribute to quantitative research efforts in the field of HIV epidemiology and prevention
Apply statistical models and use statistical software to derive quantitative research findings
Work as part of a team to develop scientific data from various data sources
Contribute as co-author to manuscripts
Contribute to data visualization output to disseminate study findings

The position will be based at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia. The initial appointment is for 2 years, and renewal is anticipated if performance is satisfactory and funds remain available.

Detailed Project Description:

PREMISE

To reach Ending the Epidemic (ETE) targets, we will need consistent national HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) data to describe patterns of use and to understand which programs and policies are effective at facilitating PrEP uptake. This NIH-funded study aims to build on our history of developing public PrEP data resources and innovative metrics of PrEP use in PREMISE (PrEP Epidemiology, Modeling, and Surveillance), a collaborative and interdisciplinary group that will use national PrEP data, along with legal and policy coding, to inform the US HIV epidemic response. The study will conduct analyses regarding the scope of PrEP scale-up over time and will perform analyses to explore the impact of different locality-specific programs and policies on PrEP use

MISTR+

Our study (MISTR+) seeks to establish an evidence base for telehealth and improve health outcomes in terms of PrEP care initiation, retention, and re-engagement for the over 100,000 users of this service by (1) developing a series of low-touch interventions based on existing evidence and new data analyses of telePrEP electronic records data, (2) testing interventions, and (3) enhancing our understanding of intervention performance through machine learning and cost-effectiveness analysesthat will inform intervention prioritization.

Elección

The HIV epidemic in Latin America is concentrated among MSM. As the number of HIV prevention options grows, it is critical to build interventions that empower individuals to make HIV prevention choices that fit their lives; this requires delineating and addressing barriers, elucidating individual preferences, and providing accessible prevention options. Remote access to health services and information may overcome many challenges of traditional clinic service delivery models. TheElección study will improve our understanding of health determinants for HIV incidence and the prevention and care cascades in Peru. The study will build a cohort to assess HIV incidence and its predictors and to identify intervention preferences. We will adapt and test a digital intervention grounded in participant choice to improve HIV prevention service uptake. Specifically, we will develop an observational HIV incidence cohort (Aim 1), implement discrete choice experiments and use the ADAPT-ITT model to inform adaptation of an evidence-based intervention to the Peruvian setting (Aim 2), and transition cohort members into the clinical trial (Aim 3). Participants will be randomized to either the adapted version of the digital intervention (M-Cubicado) or to observation-only follow-up (standard of care).

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

A bachelor's degree and one year of experience in data analysis, statistics, or a related field, OR an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Master’s degree in Epidemiology, Biostatistics or other relevant quantitative field.
Experience with quantitative data analysis.
Experience using statistical software to derive quantitative research findings.
Excellent scientific writing ability
Experience in data management and analysis using SAS, R or other statistical software.
Experience in analysis of clinical trial and/or national claims data.
Experience in HIV prevention or digital health

Schedule is based on agreed upon guidelines of department. This role requires residency in the state of GA. Emory reserves the right to change remote work status with notice to employee.

Overview

Since our founding in 1924, we've cut cardiovascular disease deaths in half, but there is still so much more to do. To overcome today’s biggest health challenges and accelerate this progress, we need passionate individuals like you. Join our movement, be part of the progress, and help ensure a healthier future for all. You matter, and so does the impact you can make with us.

The American Heart Association has an excellent opportunity for a Project Coordinator in our Quality, Outcome Research, & Analytics (QORA) department!

This is a full-time, benefits-eligible, grant-funded opportunity. Current funding will expire April 1, 2027 with the possibility of extension.

This position can be home-based.

The Association offers many resources to help you maintain work-life harmonization through your changing needs and life situations. To help you be successful, you will have access to Heart U, our award-winning corporate university, as well as additional training and support, locally.

\#TheAHALife is more than a company culture; it is our way of life. It embodies our commitment to work-life harmonization and is guided by our core values where our employees can thrive both personally and professionally. Discover why you will Be Seen. Be Heard. Be Valued at the American Heart Association by following us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, and at heart.jobs.

Responsibilities

The Project Coordinator supports the successful execution of health sciences research and measure development initiatives through project coordination, administrative support, stakeholder engagement, and program operations. Working closely with internal staff, subject matter experts, researchers, and external partners, this role coordinates meetings and activities, maintains project documentation and databases, supports reporting efforts, and ensures smooth day-to-day operations.

Support day-to-day operations of initiatives, including scheduling internal, external, and cross-functional meetings, managing agendas, capturing notes and action items, tracking follow-up activities, coordinating materials, and maintaining project documentation.
Develop, input, and maintain information in project tracking systems, databases, SharePoint sites, and other software platforms.
Handle administrative and financial tasks, including processing invoices, tracking budgets and expenses, and supporting contract and grant administration activities.
Support virtual meeting logistics and technology setup.
Serve as a primary point of contact for project participants, subject matter experts, and external partners, coordinating communications, responding to inquiries, and assisting with onboarding activities.
Prepare and maintain project documentation, status reports, meeting summaries, dashboards, stakeholder updates, and other materials aligned with project goals and timelines.
Assist with the development and dissemination of program materials, templates, reports, and resources.
Coordinate project timelines, deliverables, and meeting schedules to support successful execution of research and measure development activities.

Qualifications

High School Diploma or equivalent.
Minimum of three (3) years of relevant experience that includes administrative and/or project coordination experience.
Ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously and meet specified timelines.
Administrative expertise with sophisticated clerical responsibilities and data management.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.
Effective interpersonal skills with proven ability to develop collaborative working relationships internally and externally.
Experience coordinating meetings, events, or project activities across multiple stakeholder groups.

Here are some of the preferred experience and skills we are seeking:

Bachelor's degree in health sciences, public health, healthcare administration, research, or a related field.
Experience supporting health sciences, research, quality improvement, measurement, or healthcare-related projects.
Experience working with subject matter experts, researchers, healthcare professionals, or external partners.
Knowledge of basic data tracking, reporting, or research support processes.

Proficiency Requirement

Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint. Experience working with project management, database, or collaboration systems is a plus.

Compensation & Benefits

The expected pay range will be $20.51 per hour to $25.64 per hour. Pay is commensurate with experience; geographic differentials to the pay range may apply. The American Heart Association reserves the right to pay more or less than the posted range. The American Heart Association invests in its people. Here are the main components of our total rewards package. Visit Rewards & Benefits to see more details.

Compensation – Our goal is to ensure you have a competitive base salary. That’s why we regularly review the market value of jobs and make adjustments, as needed.
Performance and Recognition – You are rewarded for achieving success through annual salary planning and incentive programs; eligibility for an incentive program is based on the type of position.
Benefits – We offer a wide array of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance, along with a robust retirement program that includes an employer match and automatic contribution. As a mark of our commitment to employee well-being, we also offer an employee assistance program, employee wellness program and telemedicine, and medical consultation.

Work-Life Harmonization – The Association offers Paid Time Off (PTO) at a minimum of 16 days per year for new employees. The number of days will increase based on seniority level. You will also have a total of 12 paid holidays off each year, which includes several days off at the end of the year.
Tuition Assistance - We support the career development of all employees. This program provides financial assistance to employees who wish to further their education and career in relation to their current duties and responsibilities, or for potential future positions in the organization.

The American Heart Association’s 2028 Goal: Building on over 100 years of trusted leadership in cardiovascular and brain health, by 2028 the Association will drive breakthroughs and implement proven solutions in science, policy, and care for healthier people and communities. The greatest discoveries in health must reach everyone where they are.

At American Heart Association | American Stroke Association, our mission is to be a relentless force for a world of longer, healthier lives, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, religion, age, language, sexual orientation, national origin and physical or cognitive abilities.
